title: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (pressure chamber)
what: You breathe oxygen in a special chamber with raised pressure. This helps oxygen reach your tissues better.
why: For wounds that heal poorly, diabetic foot, carbon monoxide poisoning, decompression sickness and after radiation - as prescribed by a doctor.
duration: a session usually takes 60 to 120 minutes; a course is from a few to dozens of sessions
tell_doctor: A cold, a blocked nose or ear pain
A pacemaker or other devices in your body

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Cotton clothes are usually provided. Synthetic fabric can spark.

prepare.title: Not allowed
prepare.text: You must not take a phone, lighter, electronics, oil-based cosmetics or hairspray into the chamber.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Have a light meal before the session. Do not smoke - it reduces the benefit.

steps: You enter the chamber and lie or sit down
The pressure is raised slowly - your ears feel blocked, like on a plane
You breathe oxygen through a mask or hood; in a single-person chamber the whole chamber is filled with oxygen
Staff are in contact with you the whole time
At the end the pressure is lowered slowly
feel: Blocked ears as the pressure rises - swallowing or yawning helps
It may be warm in the chamber
after: You can go back to your usual activities right away
Come to all the sessions of the course
red_flags: Severe ear pain or discharge from the ear
A change in vision that does not go away
Seizures, severe shortness of breath or chest pain - call your local emergency number

faq.q: Is it like on a plane?
faq.a: Similar: your ears block when the pressure changes. Swallow or yawn and it gets easier.

faq.q: Why can't I take my phone?
faq.a: There is a lot of oxygen in the chamber. Any spark is dangerous, so electronics stay outside.

reminders.text: Pressure chamber session in 2 hours. Cotton clothes, no cosmetics, leave your phone outside.
